title: Which pairs of angles at a crossing are linear pairs?
description: Two lines cross and the four angles are named round the crossing. The board lists the neighbouring pairs that make linear pairs, then the facing pairs that are vertically opposite, and checks the count by the neighbours of each angle.
teaching_notes: One idea: neighbours on a straight line are linear pairs, and angles facing each other are vertically opposite. Watch for students who call a facing pair a linear pair.

video_script.why: The child knows both words and now uses them on a crossing with named angles.
video_script.substitution: Go round the crossing and list each neighbouring pair, then list each facing pair, the same way as the example in the book.
video_script.anchor: Two lines crossing, with the four angles named a, b, c and d going round the crossing and a and b neighbours.
video_script.payoff_line: Four angles make four linear pairs and two vertically opposite pairs.

final_answer.value: Linear pairs: a and b, b and c, c and d, d and a. Vertically opposite pairs: a and c, b and d
final_answer.spoken: four linear pairs and two vertically opposite pairs

hold_back: Linear pairs: a and b, b and c, c and d, d and a. Vertically opposite pairs: a and c, b and d
maths_rules: linear pairs are neighbours on a straight line: a and b, b and c, c and d, d and a
vertically opposite pairs face each other across the crossing: a and c, b and d
each angle has two neighbours and one angle facing it
four angles give four neighbouring pairs and two facing pairs
the slip: a and c face each other and share no arm, so they are not a linear pair
video_script.design: One crossing stays on the stage all video. The neighbouring pairs light up one after another, then the facing pairs in a second colour.
